advice: Propose a loop-order experiment that transposes B inside gemm, then computes output in row-major order with loops `i`, `j` in small contiguous blocks, and `k` innermost: `sum += A[i*n+k] * Bt[j*n+k]`. This keeps each reduction sequential, accesses both reduction inputs contiguously, and writes C contiguously. Compare against the current SME variants to learn whether simple cache-friendly scalar/vectorizable loop ordering can offset the loss of SME outer products. Keep full FP32 arithmetic and handle all n tails; allocate and free Bt inside gemm. The supplied evidence does not establish this will be faster.
risks: This is an unmeasured design proposal. It may be much slower than SME MOPA because it gives up matrix outer-product instructions; transposing B adds timed work and allocation. Compiler reassociation under the fixed fast-math flags can also affect error, so check every output against the fixed 0.002 error limit. Verify n<=0, odd dimensions, and general sizes, and confirm the declared ABI and full k reduction are preserved.
